# Draft:The Making of a Moment

----
The Making of a Moment is a 2026 American documentary film directed by Phabian “S-Quire” Winfield. The film examines Winfield’s personal and creative journey leading up to and following a 2025 viral incident in which an NYPD detective appeared in one of his music videos. While public attention focused on the officer, the documentary centers on Winfield’s dual identity as both a federal officer and an independent hip-hop artist. The film premiered at the SVA Theatre in New York City in 2025 before its streaming release in 2026.
Synopsis
The Making of a Moment follows rapper and filmmaker Phabian “S-Quire” Winfield as he recounts the events surrounding a viral 2025 music video that featured an NYPD detective dancing on camera. Although the public discussion centered on the officer, the film shifts focus to Winfield’s personal experiences, exploring how the moment unexpectedly drew national attention to his own life.
The documentary opens with reflections on Winfield’s upbringing in Hempstead, Long Island, his Puerto Rican and African-American heritage, and his formative experiences in music. Through photographs, archival material, and extended interviews, Winfield discusses how creativity shaped his identity and provided stability during challenges in his environment.
The film then examines Winfield’s career in federal law enforcement, highlighting the internal conflict of balancing public artistic expression with professional responsibilities. As the narrative progresses, Winfield provides insight into the aftermath of the viral incident, the assumptions made by the public, and the pressures that followed from both the creative community and his role in government service.
An interview with WBLS radio host Lenny Green and commentary from individuals familiar with Winfield’s story expand on the cultural context surrounding the incident. The documentary explores broader themes of identity, faith, public perception, and the complexities of living between two distinct worlds.
Production
The documentary was produced independently through RITENOWMUZIC LLC. Filming and cinematography were handled by Michael Albanese, who also served as the project’s editor. Production incorporated sit-down interviews, personal archives, and footage filmed in New York, creating a narrative that connects Winfield’s early life, artistic career, and public exposure following the viral moment.
According to media coverage at the time, the viral incident generated significant public attention and became a defining catalyst for the film’s development, prompting Winfield to address aspects of his life that had previously remained private.
Release
Premiere
The film held its premiere screening at the SVA Theatre in New York City in 2025. The event included a private invited audience and served as the documentary’s first public showing.
Streaming
Following its premiere, the film was distributed by Filmhub and made available on streaming platforms, including Tubi, in 2026.
Reception
Media attention surrounding the events depicted in the film contributed to its visibility. Outlets such as TMZ, Complex, New York Daily News, New York Post, Vibe, and HotNewHipHop reported on the incident involving the NYPD detective, which forms a central thread of the documentary’s narrative.
While the documentary itself did not initially receive traditional film criticism, the broader narrative explored in the film has been discussed across news articles and social commentary, providing contextual reception to the themes addressed.
